relevance_note: Single adult case report with a TNFAIP3 variant, tested in relatives: "Heterozygous variant in TNFAIP3 gene c.63A>T(p. I21 = ) was detected by genetic testing from the samples of the patient, his father and his sister."
method_note: Hand extraction from the text; a short script in the scratch directory assembled the JSON and checked spans. No tables in the paper. Scope: the index patient plus three tested relatives (father and sister carry the variant and are described as without any discomfort; mother tested negative, so she has an individuals row but no variant row). The paper calls the diagnosis PFAPA syndrome, not HA20, and classifies the variant (c.63A>T, p.I21=, exon 2) as a variant of uncertain significance; it is in scope as a TNFAIP3 variant. The variant is printed in several forms (c.63A>T (P.I21=); c.63A>T(p. I21 = ) with thin spaces; c.63 A > T); the figure-legend form was used. variant_type 'other' is based on the authors' statement that the variant makes no difference in amino acid composition (no class word such as synonymous is printed). Inheritance of the patient's variant recorded as inherited paternal from the legend (father and sister carry it, mother does not). Pathogenicity for father and sister taken from the sentence naming the variant classification together with the father's and sister's samples. Contradiction: the Discussion says 'no skin changes', but the case describes red papules on the left thigh and a herpes zoster rash during admission; both rows emitted and the skin-lesions checklist item set to not reported. Normal investigations recorded as the paper names them (colonoscopy, chest CT, PET-CT, ferritin/autoantibody profile); colonoscopy does not exclude the broader GI item and chest CT does not exclude interstitial lung disease, so those checklist items stay not reported. 'No recurrent vulva ulcer' (male patient, as printed) is narrower than genital ulcers, so that checklist item stays not reported. Herpes zoster and COVID-19 are single infections, so recurrent infections stays not reported. Age 25 is the age at presentation (admission October 2022); follow-up continued about 4 more months; recorded as age at last evaluation. Diagnoses ruled out by the authors (leukemia, malignancy, SLE, Behcet disease, adult Still disease) were not recorded as features. 'father of patient' and 'sister of patient' given is_proband false; the father and sister 'without any discomfort' rows are a general statement, so no specific checklist item is excluded for them.
